summary: How wealthy American conservatives, spurred by the 1971 Powell Memorandum, funded a network of think tanks that manufactured the look of expert consensus, attacked public universities and supplied the Reagan administration with policy.

evidence.note: Russell Sage Foundation, founded 1907, presented as one of the first think tanks
RAND Corporation introduced; long segment on its Vietnam advice follows
RAND researcher interviews prisoners and villagers in Vietnam on enemy morale
RAND's ladder of escalation and bombing assumptions in the Vietnam War
Powell writes his 1971 memo to the Chamber of Commerce
Reagan's 1966 governor campaign built on attacking Berkeley
Reagan pushes tuition plus loans at California public colleges
Heritage (1973), EPPC (1976) and Cato (1977) founded in quick succession
AEI founder Lewis Brown ran an asbestos firm and hid asbestosis from workers
Kirkpatrick's AEI essay shapes Reagan's Latin America arms policy
think tanks back Reagan's Strategic Defense Initiative
closing segment on think tanks losing influence in the Trump years

notes: No theme for think tanks or policy capture; propaganda-media (manufacturing consensus for journalists) is the closest primary. Primary subject is the think-tank network as a movement, so roles are empty. Covered span starts with the 1907 Russell Sage Foundation history; end 1989 (end of the Reagan era) is an estimate, with later SDI and Trump-era remarks treated as legacy.
